resale_co.how_to_apply: No Township resale Certificate of Continued Occupancy. The Township's building FAQ says only the smoke detector, carbon monoxide (and fire extinguisher) certification from the Fire Bureau is needed for the resale of a home (see fire certificate).

evidence.quote: Does Wall Township require an inspection by the building department on resale of a home?
No. We do not require a Certificate of Continued Occupancy on the resale of home.
No. As long as the tank is still being used and it is not leaking it may remain in place.

resale_co.notes: The Building Department's "Selling your home" FAQ (PDF linked from the Building Department page) says the Township does not require a Certificate of Continued Occupancy on resale and that only the smoke detector, carbon monoxide and fire extinguisher certification is needed. The same FAQ says the Township will not make a seller remove a working, non-leaking underground oil tank and will not make a seller bring the house up to current code. The FAQ's fire phone (732-449-8444 x 254) is older; the Fire Bureau now lists (732) 820-4854. Landlord registration and the transient rental license apply to rentals only.

requirements: Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Certificate of Compliance before any residential unit is sold or changes occupancy
Battery-only smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed units; hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Smoke alarm type depends on the year built (for example, homes from March 1991 on need interconnected hardwired alarms on all levels and in each bedroom with battery back-up)
Smoke alarm near every bedroom door; basement and non-sleeping levels near the stairway to the floor above
Carbon monoxide alarm on each sleeping level near every bedroom door in homes with a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage
Central station monitored alarm systems must be certified by a licensed NJ Fire Protection Contractor before the inspection
Secondary power source (for example solar or battery storage) labeling checked under P.L.2025, c.19 when applicable
Portable fire extinguisher (the Township FAQ and the uninhabitable transfer form still list it)

authorities.name: Wall Township Fire Bureau (Fire Prevention Bureau, governed by the Joint Board of Fire Commissioners of Fire Districts 1, 2 and 3)
authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on business days before closing: more than 5 business days for the lower fee. Staff call within one business day after an online application to schedule.

fees.label: Smoke/CO certificate, initial inspection more than 5 business days before closing
fees.quote: More than 5 business days before closing: $75.

fees.label: Initial inspection 5 or fewer days before closing
fees.quote: Five or fewer days before closing: $125.

fees.label: First reinspection (more than 5 days / 5 or fewer days before closing)
Missed appointment or no entry
fees.quote: A fee of $30 will be charged for failure to maintain the scheduled appointment or entry to the structure.

fees.label: Secondary power source label inspection, when needed
fees.quote: An additional fee of $20 will be assessed in the event such an inspection is deemed necessary.

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online with the Fire Bureau's Smoke Detector Inspection Application (or email a printed application to inspection@wallfirebureau.com). Have the block, lot, address, owner, buyer, closing date and an inspection contact ready. Checks are payable to Wall Township Fire Bureau. Office: 1612 Route 71, Wall Township, NJ 07719, Monday to Friday 8am to 4pm.

evidence.quote: Pursuant to the New Jersey Uniform Fire Code, before any residential structure/unit is sold, leased, or otherwise made subject to change of occupancy the owner shall obtain a Smoke Detector & Carbon Monoxide Alarm Certificate of Compliance.
Once received, a staff member will contact you within one business day to schedule the inspection.
Completed applications can be emailed to inspection@wallfirebureau.com

The fee for any CSACMAC and issuance of a certificate, as defined and required by N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3, will be indexed to the scheduled inspection date as it relates to the anticipated contract closing date as follows:
A Smoke Detector, Carbon Monoxide and Fire Extinguisher Certification is required and is performed by the Fire Prevention Department
The Joint Board of Fire Commissioners governs the Wall Township Fire Bureau.
Fee $75/$125 (please make checks payable to: Wall Township Fire Bureau)

fire_cert.notes: Fees are in Township Code 113-3G(2)(b) (Fire Prevention), last amended 6-23-2026 by Ord. No. 15-2026, read through the ecode360 print view; the code's fee table counts days between the scheduled inspection and the anticipated closing date. Active volunteer firefighters and first aid members selling their primary residence can be exempt from the certificate fee (not reinspections). The Fire Bureau's current pages do not mention a fire extinguisher, but the Township FAQ and the uninhabitable transfer of title form still do; the state dropped the extinguisher from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19), so confirm with the Bureau. The LEA registry notes "Wall Twp is now part of Dist 3"; the DCA directory shows one Fire Bureau (LEAID 1352-003) for all three districts. The Fire Bureau website (wallfirebureau.com) is linked from the Township's Code Enforcement page.

other_items.label: Final water/sewer meter reading
other_items.detail: The Township's forms page offers a Final Meter Reading Request for sales and tenant changes (online form).

other_items.label: Uninhabitable home transfer of title
other_items.detail: If the house is uninhabitable, the Fire Bureau has a Transfer of Title for a Residential Property form ($75/$125); the home cannot be occupied until the Building Department issues a Certificate of Occupancy.
